installation.note: rsync is installed by default on most Linux distributions

overview.summary: rsync synchronizes files and directories efficiently. It only transfers differences, making it much faster than scp for large transfers or when files already exist. Supports compression, resume, and preserves permissions. Essential for backups, deployments, and large file transfers.

syntax.description: Synchronize SOURCE to DESTINATION. Only transfers differences, making it efficient. Can work locally or over SSH.

misconceptions.title: rsync always copies everything
misconceptions.misconception: rsync transfers all files every time
misconceptions.reality: rsync only transfers differences - if files are identical, nothing is transferred. This makes it very efficient for repeated syncs.
misconceptions.tip: rsync is smart - only transfers what changed. Much faster than scp for repeated transfers or large directories.

common_pitfalls.description: rsync -av source/ dest/ vs rsync -av source dest/ behave differently
common_pitfalls.solution: source/ copies contents, source copies directory itself. Be consistent: use trailing slash for 'contents of'.
Always use -n (dry run) first with --delete to see what would be deleted. Very important!

related_commands.relationship: File transfer; scp for simple copy, rsync for efficient sync

best_practices: Use -n (dry run) first to preview changes
Use -P to see progress on large transfers
Use trailing slash consistently: source/ means contents
performance_tips: rsync is very efficient - only transfers differences
Much faster than scp for large transfers or repeated syncs
Use -z for compression over slow networks

additional_notes.efficiency: rsync only transfers differences - very efficient for repeated syncs or large directories
additional_notes.trailing_slash: source/ copies contents, source copies directory. Be consistent with trailing slashes.
additional_notes.common_patterns: Very common: rsync -av source/ dest/ (sync), rsync -avz user@server:/path/ local/ (remote), rsync -av --delete source/ dest/ (mirror)
additional_notes.vs_scp: rsync = efficient sync (only differences), scp = simple copy (transfers everything). Use rsync for large/repeated transfers.
